title: Shooting of machete-wielding man by Windsor police not excessive, says SIU
article: A Windsor police officer who fatally shot a machete-wielding senior citizen in downtown Windsor in August will not face criminal charges.

The province's Special Investigations Unit has finished its extensive examination of the incident that resulted in the death of a 70-year-old local man, with the determination that the officer's actions constituted "reasonable defensive force."

According to a release on Tuesday, SIU director Joseph Martino found no reason to conclude that the officer who shot the man acted excessively "when he chose to meet an imminent lethal threat with a resort to lethal force of his own."
"I am satisfied that the (subject officer) fired his gun to protect himself and his partner," Martino wrote in his decision.
"The complainant was within two to three metres of the (subject officer) at the time, machete raised above his head, having given every indication that he was determined to assault the officers."
The incident took place on Aug. 15 at the intersection of Ouellette Avenue and Wyandotte Street.
Allan Andkilde, 70, walked with a cane. He arrived in the area shortly after 2 p.m., at which time he visited some stores and purchased a machete with a 20-centimetre blade.
At around 2:20 p.m., the man tossed his cane aside, drew the machete from its bag, and called police - informing them of his location and his weapon.

"The complainant was of unsound mind at the time and had been contemplating suicide," the SIU noted in its narrative of the incident. "It seems the complainant was intent on provoking a confrontation with the police."

A surveillance camera recorded the man as he entered the intersection, raised the machete, and pounded his chest with his free hand. He challenged traffic with the weapon, and vehicles had to swerve to avoid him.
Two Windsor police officers on bicycles were the first to arrive at the scene, reaching the intersection around 2:25 p.m.
Another surveillance camera recorded one of the officers dismounting his bicycle, drawing his firearm, and backing up. His partner drew her Taser and also immediately began backing up.
The SIU said the officers repeatedly ordered the man to drop the machete.
The man could be seen walking towards the two officers with the weapon raised in what the SIU described as "a striking position."
As the man approached the officers, he struck a stopped pickup truck with the machete.
The second police officer fired her Taser at the man - which stopped him only momentarily. According to the SIU, the man appeared to be "unaffected by the (conducted energy weapon) discharge."
As the man continued his approach, the first police officer again yelled at him to put down the machete, then fired once into the man's right abdomen.
A total of 20 seconds elapsed between the time the officer dismounted his bicycle and when he fired his handgun.
Upon being shot, the man immediately dropped the machete and fell to the ground. The officers kicked the machete away and handcuffed the man, then attempted to administer first aid.
The officers reported that the man told them to stop their efforts, and indicated he had a "Do Not Resuscitate" order in his wallet.
The man was transported for hospital for emergency surgery, but succumbed to his wound and was pronounced dead at 8:17 p.m.

"On my assessment of the evidence, there are no reasonable grounds to believe that the (subject officer) committed a criminal offence in connection with the complainant's death," Martino wrote in his decision.
"The machete ... was ostensibly capable of inflicting grievous bodily harm or death, had the complainant been allowed to advance any closer and swing it at the officers."
"The complainant had been given a reasonable opportunity to drop the machete, but refused to do so."
Further retreat or withdrawal by the officers was not an available option, Martino wrote.
"The incident occurred at a busy intersection with plenty of third-parties who would have been placed at continuing risk from the complainant had the officers not intervened."
The incident was the third time since 2018 that the SIU has investigated a Windsor police officer shooting an individual.
